Lemma po_cls_rep (k : Fin.t po_apex) : po_cls (fin_select po_isrep k) = k. — with `Definition po_apex : nat := fin_countP po_isrep` (406, the number of parts) and `Definition po_cls (p : Fin.t (y + z)) : Fin.t po_apex := fin_rank po_isrep (po_lab p) (po_isrep_lab p)` (420, the class map). statement_record.book: For a set A the set of ALL partitions of A is preordered by fineness: P is finer than Q when every part of P is contained in some part of Q. Equivalently, through the surjection presentation of Example 1.26, a surjection f : A ↠ P is finer than g : A ↠ Q exactly when there exists h : P → Q with h ∘ f = g. This is the order used on the five three-point systems of display (1.5).

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Product (C D : Category) : Category := {| obj := C * D; hom := fun x y => (fst x ~> fst y) * (snd x ~> snd y); homset := ... (componentwise ≈) ...; id := fun _ => (id, id); compose := fun _ _ _ f g => (fst f ∘ fst g, snd f ∘ snd g); ... |} — notated `C ∏ D` (line 142). The hom is the PAIR of component homs, i.e. the componentwise conjunction of the two relations; instantiated at two Prosets this is verbatim the example's definition (p, q) ≤ (p', q') iff p ≤ p' in P and q ≤ q' in Q, and the identity/composition fields discharge reflexivity and transitivity componentwise (the example's implicit content). The product remains thin, since each factor's hom-setoid is `fun _ _ => True`.

Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| Setoid.equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := fun x => @reflexivity A R (@PreOrder_Reflexive A R P) x; compose := fun x y z f g => @transitivity A R (@PreOrder_Transitive A R P) x y z g f |} — the bridge that makes the previous entry apply to the example: a preorder IS a (thin) category, its identities reflexivity and its composition transitivity, so `Proset P ∏ Proset Q` is the product preorder of P and Q.

statement_record.book: Given preorders P and Q, the product set P × Q carries the product preorder defined componentwise: (p, q) ≤ (p', q') iff p ≤ p' in P and q ≤ q' in Q. Flagged by the book as a basic instance of the more general product of categories.
statement_record.intree: Definition Product (C D : Category) : Category := {| obj := C * D; hom := fun x y => (fst x ~> fst y) * (snd x ~> snd y); ... id := (id, id); compose := (fst f ∘ fst g, snd f ∘ snd g) |}, notated C ∏ D; with Proset turning a PreOrder into a thin category.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the library proves exactly the generalization the book points at (the product of ARBITRARY categories, with functoriality of the projections Fst/Snd at Construction/Product.v:150/158 and the swap at 166, and the whole bifunctor apparatus riding on it), and the preorder case is its instance at Proset with no side condition. The only presentational difference is that the in-tree conjunction is a pair-TYPE `(f, g)` rather than a Prop conjunction — faithful under the library's Type-valued hom convention — and no in-tree lemma names `Proset P ∏ Proset Q` as 'the product preorder' (the specialization is definitional, requiring no proof).

This is the example verbatim once read through Proset: the SAME objects (obj := @obj C) with the relation reversed (hom x y := hom C y x), and the category laws — i.e. reflexivity and transitivity of the reversed relation — are discharged from those of C, which is exactly the example's parenthetical 'reflexivity and transitivity are inherited'.

Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| Setoid.equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := fun x => @reflexivity A R (@PreOrder_Reflexive A R P) x; compose := fun x y z f g => @transitivity A R (@PreOrder_Transitive A R P) x y z g f |} — makes the previous entry apply: a preorder is a thin category, so `(Proset P)^op` is a category on the same carrier A whose hom is `fun x y => R y x`, i.e. the opposite preorder p ≤ q iff q ≤ p in P.

statement_record.book: Given a preorder P, the opposite preorder P^op has the same underlying set with the order reversed: p ≤ q in P^op exactly when q ≤ p in P (reflexivity and transitivity being inherited).
statement_record.intree: Definition Opposite (C : Category) : Category := {| obj := @obj C; hom := fun x y => @hom C y x; id := @id C; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f; id_left := @id_right; comp_assoc := comp_assoc_sym; ... |}, notated C^op; with Proset presenting a preorder as a thin category.
